A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new key-value caching architecture that is tightly integrated with the underlying flash storage, so that the key-value cache system can take full advantage of the unique properties of flash devices, such as high density, low power consumption and non-volatility.
we propose a new cache system, DIDACache, which integrates device and application for flash-based key-value caching.

we have built a key-value caching system that is designed from the ground up for SSDs, and we have shown that such a system can achieve significant performance improvement over the existing solutions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we can significantly boost the performance and efficiency of flash-based key-value caches by closing the semantic gap and designing a system that is aware of the underlying flash devices’ characteristics and constraints.

the performance gap between DRAM- and flash-based cache systems can be greatly reduced with careful integration of the cache manager and the device, and that the performance gap can be further reduced by exploiting the device-level parallelism.

we can significantly improve the performance and reduce the energy consumption of flash-based key-value caching by integrating the key-value cache management with the underlying flash devices, which we call the device and application integration (DAI).
